negative_findings.description: nbrm.mk (National Bank of RNM) returned HTTP 403 Forbidden to WebFetch on the payment-system-operators register URL; the same defence is assumed for the e-money register and licensing pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: Register pages are indexed by search engines and clearly live, but not retrievable by plain fetch. Treated as bot-defended-but-live, NOT dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single most authoritative list of licensed PIs/EMIs and payment-system operators in this cell needs a headless-browser or header-spoofing collector, otherwise the actor map will silently go stale.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated MK 'people moves' / appointments column covering non-bank payments companies was found in either mk or en searches.
negative_findings.result_summary: Leadership news for KIBS/CaSys/PSPs appears only sporadically and incidentally across faktor.mk, bankarstvo.mk, ecommerce.mk interviews and LinkedIn.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Leadership-move detection for this cell must be reconstructed from Central Registry filings plus scattered media, not from a single feed — raises collection cost and latency.

coverage_gaps.description: The full licensed population of MK payment institutions and e-money institutions under the 2022 Law was not enumerated, because the NBRSM registers could not be fetched. Only four PSP/EMI actors were confirmed by name in media: Paysera Македонија, Iute Pay, Flex Pay (Флекс пеј), plus foreign entrant Nayax.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a headless-browser pass over the NBRSM e-money-institution, payment-institution and payment-system-operator registers to extract the complete entity list, then seed a Central Registry watchlist from it.

coverage_gaps.description: No MK-specific general job board (e.g. vrabotuvanje.com.mk, pazar3.mk, mojarabota-type portals) was verified in this pass as carrying payments-sector vacancies; only fakulteti.mk and bankarstvo.mk were observed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Dedicated mk-language pass on 'вработување', 'слободни работни места', 'оглас' portals filtered to the payments employer watchlist.

coverage_gaps.description: Bank-owned or telco-owned wallet/e-money ventures (Halkbank Skopje wallet, A1/Telekom-linked payment ventures, mPay/CPay-style wallets) were not confirmed as MK entities in this pass — the mPay hit was a non-MK app.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Targeted mk searches on 'мобилен паричник', 'дигитален паричник', 'електронски паричник' plus each bank/telco name; verify against the NBRSM EMI register once retrievable.

coverage_gaps.description: Annual reports / годишни извештаи of KIBS and CaSys (which list management and supervisory board composition year by year) were not located.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch the entities' own annual reports and any Macedonian Stock Exchange (МСЕ / berza.com.mk) disclosures, since KIBS is a joint-stock company (АД) with governance-disclosure obligations.

coverage_gaps.description: Albanian-language MK media were out of declared scope and therefore uncovered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: If scope is widened, add portalb.mk and koha.mk with sq payments/hiring terms.

brief: North Macedonia's payments-ecosystem labour market has three distinct source layers. The authoritative layer is regulatory and registry-based — the NBRSM registers of e-money institutions, payment institutions and payment-system operators, plus the Central Registry (crm.com.mk) whose управител/board change filings are the only legal ground truth for leadership moves — but nbrm.mk is bot-defended (HTTP 403 on plain fetch) and CRM is partly fee-based, so both need engineered collectors rather than simple crawls. The company layer is thin but high-value: KIBS AD Skopje and КаСис/CaSys are the two infrastructure employers, joined since the 2022 Law on Payment Services by a young licensed PSP/EMI population (Paysera Македонија, Iute Pay, Флекс пеј) and foreign entrants such as Nayax. The media layer carries most of the early signal and is almost entirely Macedonian-language — bankarstvo.mk (which reprints payments job ads verbatim), faktor.mk (board/governance churn at KIBS), mkd.mk and pari.com.mk (licence grants), and ecommerce.mk interviews that reliably pin name-to-title for payments executives; there is no dedicated MK appointments column for non-bank payments, so leadership tracking must be reconstructed rather than subscribed to.
